query: If the most common operational burdens described in the text were eliminated, how much would resolution duration drop?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The nature of the incident (database, email, vpn) is not itself an intervenable operational burden, but it is a common cause of both which burdens arise and how long resolution takes. Acts as a confounder to adjust for, not named in the query.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom type (cannot_connect, access_denied) is an intrinsic characteristic of the incident affecting both the burdens encountered and duration; not settable, so a confounder rather than treatment. Not named in query.

per_column.name: server_vs_client_locus
per_column.rationale: Where the fault resides influences the operational burden and the time to resolve; an immutable property of the incident, so a confounder. Not named.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether an issue is individual vs system-wide is a common cause of both handling burden and duration; not intervenable, so a confounder. Not named.

per_column.name: reassigned_resolver
per_column.rationale: Reassignment/hand-off is an operational burden that a process could actually eliminate or change -- an intervenable lever. This is the closest thing to a settable treatment and is also plausibly a mediator of duration.

per_column.name: off_hours_open
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket opened off-hours is a time-of-arrival attribute that is essentially fixed once it happened, but influences staffing burden and duration. Treated as a confounder rather than an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: recurring_caller_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurring caller status is a caller trait affecting both burden and duration; not directly settable. Confounder, and heavily imbalanced (497/3) so of low practical value.

judge.rationale: The query poses a what-if: eliminating common operational burdens and reading off the change in resolution_duration. Only reassigned_resolver is a genuinely intervenable operational lever (an actor could redesign routing to avoid reassignment), so a settable treatment is present. However, the column set is dominated by intrinsic incident attributes (category, symptom, locus, scope) that operationalize 'burden' as fixed characteristics rather than eliminable levers; these function as confounders but are only partially plausible and none are named in the query. off_hours_open and recurring_caller_pattern are weak (fixed/imbalanced). The set thus partially satisfies the interventional claim -- an intervenable treatment plus unnamed confounders -- but the treatment framing is thin and most 'burden' columns are non-intervenable, giving moderate confounder quality.
